pr.body:
We're adding one more step in the GitHub integration installation pipeline, namely GitHub OAuth2 authorize. This is transparent from the UX perspective as the data exchange happens without user interaction.

The pipeline will now fail in these cases:
- If there is a mismatch between currently authenticated GitHub user (derived from OAuth2 authorize step) and the user who installed the GitHub app (https://github.com/apps/sentry-io)
- If there is a mismatch between `state` parameter supplied by user and pipeline signature
- If GitHub could not generate correct `access_token` from the `code` (wrong or attempt of re-use of `code`).

In all those cases, this error is shown:
![image](https://github.com/getsentry/sentry/assets/1127549/18923861-2ead-4cf5-adda-7738aef801d7)
pr.title: fix(security): validate GitHub user during integration installation

raw_findings.body: Accessing integration.metadata["sender"] raises KeyError, producing an unhandled 500 server error instead of the intended graceful failure page.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Uncaught KeyError escapes the view and yields a 500 rather than the designed error response.
raw_findings.impact: Accessing integration.metadata["sender"] raises KeyError, producing an unhandled 500 server error instead of the intended graceful failure page.
raw_findings.root_cause: New user-mismatch check indexes metadata["sender"]["login"] without verifying that the sender key exists, though metadata sender is known to be optional.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Use integration.metadata.get("sender", {}).get("login") (or explicitly handle the missing key by returning error(...)) instead of indexing directly.
raw_findings.title: Unguarded access to integration.metadata["sender"] can raise KeyError
raw_findings.trigger: The installation flow reaches GitHubInstallation.dispatch for an ACTIVE Integration whose metadata does not contain a "sender" key (e.g. an integration created through a path that did not populate sender, as explicitly anticipated by installation.py which checks `if "sender" not in integration.metadata`).

raw_findings.body: The flow short-circuits before ever calling get_installation_info/build_integration, so the mocked 404 response is never hit; the test passes on the state-mismatch path and no longer verifies the 'installation could not be found' behavior it is named for.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Test provides false confidence by asserting a generic error message for an unrelated early-exit branch.
raw_findings.impact: The flow short-circuits before ever calling get_installation_info/build_integration, so the mocked 404 response is never hit; the test passes on the state-mismatch path and no longer verifies the 'installation could not be found' behavior it is named for.
raw_findings.root_cause: The state parameter passed does not match the pipeline signature, causing the added OAuth step to reject the request before the intended 404 code path runs.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Use the correct pipeline signature (9cae5e88803f35ed7970fc131e6e65d3) for the state so the flow reaches the 404 handling, and keep an assertion targeting that specific error, or split state-mismatch coverage into its own test.
raw_findings.title: test_installation_not_found no longer exercises the 404 branch
raw_findings.trigger: The test supplies a `state` value (ddd023d8...) that differs from the pipeline signature used elsewhere (9cae5e88...), so OAuthLoginView.dispatch returns early at the `state != pipeline.signature` check.

raw_findings.body: get_user_info calls resp.raise_for_status(), so an HTTPError propagates uncaught and produces a 500 error instead of the intended error(...) response guarded by the `if "login" not in authenticated_user_info` check, which becomes dead code for the failure case.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Unhandled exception escapes the pipeline view on a foreseeable API failure.
raw_findings.impact: get_user_info calls resp.raise_for_status(), so an HTTPError propagates uncaught and produces a 500 error instead of the intended error(...) response guarded by the `if "login" not in authenticated_user_info` check, which becomes dead code for the failure case.
raw_findings.root_cause: The graceful-failure handling assumes get_user_info returns a dict on failure, but it raises instead.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Wrap the get_user_info call in try/except and return error(request, self.active_organization) on failure, rather than relying on the subsequent 'login' membership check.
raw_findings.title: get_user_info raises on non-2xx, defeating the intended graceful 'login' check
raw_findings.trigger: The access_token exchange succeeds but the subsequent /user request returns a non-2xx status (e.g. token revoked between steps, scope/permission error, or GitHub API error).

finding.verifier_reason: The patch adds line 503 `!= integration.metadata["sender"]["login"]` which directly indexes metadata["sender"] without checking if the key exists. The repository context shows installation.py line 44 explicitly checks `if "sender" not in integration.metadata` before accessing it, proving sender is known to be optional. An Integration created via a path that doesn't populate sender (or an older integration) would raise KeyError, causing a 500 instead of the intended error() response.

finding.verifier_reason: The patch adds line 434 calling get_user_info(payload["access_token"]) and the repository context shows get_user_info (provider.py line 16) calls resp.raise_for_status() which raises HTTPError on non-2xx responses. The subsequent check `if "login" not in authenticated_user_info` on line 435 would never execute for API failures since the exception propagates first, causing a 500 instead of the graceful error() response.
